rows.why: Item 2 asks whether reading ignores letter case and surrounding whitespace. Its pick trims and lowercases the value, so "Draft" reads as draft and " PUBLISHED " as published, which is what the scenario expects.

Item 4 asks which old spellings map to which statuses. Its pick maps only "in review" to review and has no other aliases. So "under_review" and "LIVE" would read as null instead of review and published.

Item 1 asks what reading an unknown value returns. Its pick returns null and never the nearest status, which matches the scenario. Item 7 covers the empty and all-space cases and also gives null, but item 1 is the closer question.
No item asks what happens when an exact status is written. Item 5 asks only about values that are not exact enum values, so answering it would not settle this scenario.

Item 5 asks what writing a value that is not an exact enum value does, including old spellings like "in-review". Its pick throws and does not normalise, so only exact lowercase values pass. That matches the scenario. Item 6 also says the message includes the quoted value, but item 5 is the closest question.

Item 9 asks how a batch read reports unreadable values: form, de-duplication and order. Its pick lists each distinct raw string once, uncleaned and sorted, which matches the scenario. Item 8 covers keeping rows with a null status, but item 9 is the closest to the reporting this scenario is about.
